part.name: TAPERED PIN
part.material: MAT'L: STEEL LASALLE STRESS PROOF OPT'L: SAE 4140 (30-38 Rc) MIN YIELD 100,000 PSI OPT'L: ASTM A311 CLASS B GRADE 1141/1144 MIN YIELD 100,000 PSI

coordinate_system.orientation_notes: X follows the pin's axis of revolution, with the external threaded stud at the -X end and the main cylindrical body and internal threaded opening at the +X end. In the front and detail views, Y is vertical and Z is into the page; in the end view, Y is vertical and Z is horizontal. Datum A establishes the axis and radial origin, but no axial zero or clocking datum is specified.

features.name: Thread relief groove
features.description: Relief groove / neck between the external thread and the tapered body with corner radius and 21.65 deg transition angle.

features.name: Pin end face
features.description: Transverse circular end face of the tapered pin showing concentric feature outlines, annotated with CENTERS PERMISSIBLE allowing lathe center drilling.

geometry.position_description: End face normal to the pin axis

features.name: External thread 1.250-12 UNF-2A
features.description: External threaded stud on the left end with entry chamfer and major diameter position tolerance to Datum A.

features.name: Tapered body
features.description: External conical section with 1.50 in/ft taper, circular runout tolerance to Datum A, and surface finish 100 Ra.

features.name: Shoulder transition fillet
features.description: Transition radius between the tapered body and the large cylindrical body shoulder.

features.name: Main cylindrical body (Datum A)
features.description: Large outer cylindrical diameter on the right end forming Datum A, with surface finish 125 Ra and end chamfer.

features.name: Internal threaded hole .625-18 UNF-2B
features.description: Blind threaded hole drilled and tapped coaxially into the right end face of the pin.

relationships.detail: The external thread and datum cylinder share the pin's nominal X-axis centerline.
The circumferential thread relief shares the pin axis with the datum cylinder.
The tapered body and main cylindrical body share the nominal axis of revolution.
The blind internal threaded hole is explicitly described as coaxial with the pin.
The position control on the external thread major diameter references datum A, established by the main cylindrical body.
The tapered-surface runout control references datum A.
The tapered-surface runout control relates the taper to the axis established by datum A; this edge does not imply a separate concentricity tolerance.
The shoulder transition fillet joins the tapered body at their shared boundary.
The shoulder transition fillet joins the main cylindrical-body shoulder.
The internal threaded hole opens through the transverse right-end face, identified by the matching +X access direction.
The end-face plane is explicitly normal to the pin axis established by the datum cylinder. This expresses geometric orientation, not an additional GD&T control.

datums.description: Outer cylindrical surface Ø 2.130 / 2.120 on right section of pin

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: A is the sole defined datum and establishes the cylindrical datum axis. Both the external-thread position control and tapered-surface runout control reference A. No secondary or tertiary datum is specified.

assumptions.text: The explicit detail reference on front_view:F2 identifies detail_view_optional_undercut:F1 as an alternative configuration of the same shoulder-relief zone, not an additional physical groove.

front_view:F2 is canonical because it defines the baseline relief profile and its axial context. The front-view configuration is the default production interpretation; the optional detail remains a permitted alternative. Callouts from these configurations must not be enforced cumulatively.

end_view:F1 remains a singleton because the front view contains no separately extracted flat-face observation. Its +X access direction identifies it as the right-end face containing the internal threaded opening.

The explicit inch-unit note governs the dimensional values despite Stage 1 field names ending in _mm. Values are preserved unchanged by this merge and must not be treated downstream as already normalized millimetres.

Unqualified surface-finish symbols are interpreted as Ra in microinches under the inch-based drawing convention. The Stage 1 surface_finish_ra values are not assumed to have already been converted to micrometres.
